item.content:encoded:
The Yankees placed Schmidt on the 15-day injured list Thursday with right bicep neuritis, retroactive to Monday.
Schmidt's move to the injured list will officially rule him out for the AL Wild Card Series and the start of the ALDS, but there's a chance that the Yankees may shut the 30-year-old down for the season and focus on getting him ready for 2027. He appeared in just one regular-season game this year, allowing two hits and recording two strikeouts in two-thirds of an inning Sept. 16 against Minnesota. Bradley Hanner will come up to fill the open bullpen spot.

item.title: [Fox News] Why Yankees ace Cam Schlittler is in the AL MVP conversation and could join an exclusive club
item.dc:creator: Ryan Canfield
item.description: If you shoot for the moon, you will land among the stars. In Cam Schlittler’s case, however, he and his blazing fastball may take him past the stars and straight to the moon. The New York Yankees ace has been nothing short of dominant this season. The swashbuckling 25-year-old is all but a lock to win the American League Cy Young Award. But why stop there? He should win the American League MVP too. Schlittler should become just the 12th player in MLB history to win the Cy Young and MVP in the sa
item.content:encoded:
If you shoot for the moon, you will land among the stars. In Cam Schlittler’s case, however, he and his blazing fastball may take him past the stars and straight to the moon.
The New York Yankees ace has been nothing short of dominant this season. The swashbuckling 25-year-old is all but a lock to win the American League Cy Young Award.
But why stop there? He should win the American League MVP too. Schlittler should become just the 12th player in MLB history to win the Cy Young and MVP in the same season.
This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.
Heading into his final start of the year against the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday, Schlittler leads all American League pitchers in ERA (1.94) and is tied for first in WHIP with Drew Rasmussen (0.91). He has been durable, making all his starts, and is second in the AL in innings pitched (190 2/3).
With a devastating combination of cutters, sinkers and fastballs, the young right-hander has racked up 234 strikeouts, third in the AL behind Cleveland Guardians ace Gavin Williams (244) and likely Cy Young runner-up Dylan Cease (239).
Schlittler has set a Yankees franchise record by allowing one or no runs in 21 starts this year. He became just the third pitcher age 25 or younger in the live-ball era, which began in 1920, to achieve the feat, joining Dean Chance (1964) and Blake Snell (2018).
Schlittler also leads the AL in bWAR with 7.0, ahead of other MVP contenders such as Houston Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez (6.6), Kansas City Royals star Bobby Witt Jr. (6.5) and Rays phenom Junior Caminero (5.6).
The numbers for Schlittler are outstanding, but they don’t tell the full story.
Schlittler has been the pillar of the Yankees' pitching staff, which leads all of baseball with a 3.21 team ERA.
While the pitching staff has been fantastic, it has have dealt with plenty of injuries to the starting rotation.
Gerrit Cole didn’t make his season debut until May 22, as he was recovering from Tommy John surgery. Carlos Rodón began the season on the IL after undergoing surgery to remove a bone spur and loose bodies and didn’t debut until May 10. That was just his first stint on the IL. He returned to the IL on July 3 and didn’t come back until Aug. 18.
Rodón was not the only Yankees ace to land on the IL twice, as Max Fried did as well. Fried first went on the IL with a left elbow bone bruise on May 13, right after Cole returned, and was activated on July 22. He went on the IL for a second time on Aug. 17 with the same injury and returned Aug. 29.
Ryan Weathers, who had been key in stepping up during the absences of Cole, Fried and Rodón, went on the IL on Aug. 23 with a left forearm flexor strain.
For the Yankees, not only was it paramount that Schlittler make every start, but it was also essential that he remain dominant to help keep the rotation afloat.
Adding to the pressure on Schlittler and the pitching staff as a whole, the Yankees’ offense cratered after Aaron Judge was placed on the IL at the beginning of June. Since June 1, the Yankees have hit a paltry .229 with a putrid .297 on-base percentage.
The Yankees’ offensive ineptitude put further pressure on Schlittler and Co. to win games without Judge.
In 2023, the Yankees’ season went off the rails when Judge suffered a torn ligament in his toe. They went 25-31 without the captain and missed the postseason. The Yankees’ pitching staff in 2023, led by Cole, who won the AL Cy Young Award that season, had a 3.97 ERA, which was not enough to save the Yankees from finishing 82-80.
In 2026, the Yankees went 48-41 without Judge in the lineup, buoyed by the pitching staff’s excellence. Carried by the Schlittler-led pitching staff, the Yankees made the postseason and secured home-field advantage in the American League Wild Card Series.
While the Yankees didn’t catch the Tampa Bay Rays and win the American League East, they might have missed the postseason entirely if it weren’t for Schlittler.
By the award’s definition, Schlittler has been the most valuable player on his team.
Alvarez has been dominant in his own right. The hulking left-handed hitter, with a .316 batting average, 41 home runs and 102 RBI made a bid for the Triple Crown, but that seems out of reach.
Alvarez has been primarily a designated hitter, filling that role in 131 of the 154 games he played this season. Shohei Ohtani is the only player to win an MVP as a primary designated hitter, and he did so after becoming the first player to hit 50 home runs and steal 50 bases in a season.
Unless Alvarez surges to win the Triple Crown, nothing he is doing this season is unprecedented or historic.
Alvarez’s Astros, who are 78-80, might miss the postseason despite playing in the American League West, a division that has been historically bad.
Bobby Witt Jr. has been his usual superstar self but missed 11 games due to injury and has also taken a slight step back from last season while playing for the AL Central-worst Kansas City Royals.Caminero, the linchpin of the AL-leading Rays’ lineup, trails Schlittler in bWAR by more than a full win. Still, his .274 average and 41 home runs leave him in the thick of the AL MVP race.
Despite the excellence of Alvarez, Witt and Caminero, Schlittler should become the first pitcher since Justin Verlander in 2011 to win the American League MVP.
Verlander, like Schlittler this year, led the American League in bWAR with 8.6.
Without Schlittler, the Yankees do not survive Judge’s absence. When the Yankees could hardly scrape together three runs a game in the dead of summer, Schlittler made sure it was enough to hold on.
Without Schlittler’s dominance and durability, the Yankees do not have the second-best record in the American League (91-67).
Without Schlittler, Yankees fans are in a complete state of panic because they might still be trying to secure a Wild Card berth in a weak American League.
At the sportsbooks, Schlittler is a long shot to win the American League MVP. But odds be damned, the award should be his. He has landed on the moon.

item.title: [MLB.com] ¡De locura! Dieciséis datos asombrosos de la temporada del 2026
item.dc:creator: Anthony Castrovince
item.description: En el Día Inaugural de este año, los Cardenales y Rays jugaron un partido en el que cada uno anotó seis carreras o más en la sexta entrada. Apenas llevábamos unas horas en la temporada del 2026, y ya los investigadores del Elias Sports Bureau estaban buscando en los libros de récords para encontrar que un juego del 19 de abril de 1890 entre los Boston Beaneaters y los Brooklyn Bridegrooms marcó la última vez que dos escuadras habían anotado tantas rayitas en un solo inning en un partido inaugura
item.content:encoded:
En el Día Inaugural de este año, los Cardenales y Rays jugaron un partido en el que cada uno anotó seis carreras o más en la sexta entrada. Apenas llevábamos unas horas en la temporada del 2026, y ya los investigadores del Elias Sports Bureau estaban buscando en los libros de récords para encontrar que un juego del 19 de abril de 1890 entre los Boston Beaneaters y los Brooklyn Bridegrooms marcó la última vez que dos escuadras habían anotado tantas rayitas en un solo inning en un partido inaugural.
Así comenzó nuestra dosis diaria de estadísticas de locura en el béisbol.
Ahora que la campaña del 2026 está a punto de terminar, revisemos esos libros para ver cuáles números extraños de todo el año la han hecho tan especial.
(Todas las estadísticas son hasta los juegos del martes. Como de costumbre, ¡gracias a la investigadora Sarah Langs, que es increíble en el mejor de los sentidos, por su ayuda en la recopilación de esta lista!)
.673
El OPS de Pete Crow-Armstrong al llegar al primer tercio de la temporada de los Cachorros. Esto, de un muchacho que terminó registrando una temporada de 10 de fWAR (la versión de FanGraphs de Victorias por Encima del Reemplazo) y que probablemente se lleve fácilmente el premio a Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Nacional.
Nunca ha habido un giro similar. Entre los 56 jugadores anteriores en tener una campaña de 10 de fWAR, éstas fueron las marcas de OPS más bajas en el primer tercio:
Eddie Collins, Atléticos de Filadelfia de 1909: .826
Mike Trout, Angelinos del 2012: .835
Honus Wagner, Piratas de 1908: .894
Trout, Angelinos del 2013: .920
Wagner, Piratas de 1905: .924
Como pueden ver, nadie se había acercado a un OPS tan bajo como el de PCA en el primer tercio de la campaña de camino a un total de WAR tan extraordinario. PCA sólo valía 1.4 de fWAR en ese momento. Ahora, podemos decir que ha tenido posiblemente la mejor temporada individual en la historia de la no tan joven franquicia de los Cachorros. Un repunte en plena campaña para el recuerdo.
200+
Tanto Jacob Misiorowski de los Cerveceros (223) como Cam Schlittler de los Yankees (217) tienen EFE+ por encima de 200, lo que significa que han sido más del doble de buenos que el promedio de la liga. Por eso son los presuntos favoritos para los Premios Cy Young.
En primer lugar, es inusual contar con dos lanzadores con una EFE+ de al menos 200 en una sola campaña. Eso sólo ha ocurrido dos veces en una temporada completa en este siglo: En el 2015 (Jake Arrieta y Zack Greinke) y en el 2018 (Jacob deGrom y Blake Snell).
Pero lo doblemente asombroso aquí es que tanto Misiorowski como Schlittler están apenas en su segunda campaña en las Mayores. Los únicos otros monticulares en la Era de la Bola Viva (desde 1920) en tener una EFE+ de al menos 200 en su primera o segunda temporada fueron Dwight Gooden en su legendaria campaña de 1985 (229) y Paul Skenes en su año del Cy Young en el 2025 (226).
81
Victorias para los Medias Blancas. Eso es por mucho la mayor cantidad para un equipo después de tres temporadas consecutivas de 100 derrotas o más. El récord anterior había sido de 70, logrado por los Astros del 2014, los Senadores de Washington de 1965 y los Bravos de Boston de 1925.
Ningún equipo ha clasificado para los playoffs después de siquiera dos campañas seguidas de 100 derrotas. Los Patipálidos podrían convertirse en los primeros.
106
Bases por bolas para el cañonero cubano de los Astros, Yordan Álvarez -- la mayor cantidad en las Mayores.
Si Álvarez de alguna manera puede conseguir la Triple Corona de la Liga Americana en estos días finales (necesita superar a Pete Alonso por el título de impulsadas), no sólo sería el primero en lograr esa hazaña en cualquiera de las ligas desde el venezolano Miguel Cabrera en el 2012. También sería apenas el segundo jugador en ganar una Triple Corona y a la vez liderar la liga en bases por bolas. Ted Williams lo hizo en 1942 y 1947.
Para los niños que nos leen: Ustedes quieren batear como Ted Williams. Eso es algo bueno.
16
El número de jugadores esta temporada que han dado jonrón en su debut en MLB. Es un nuevo récord, tres más que el tope anterior establecido en el 2022.
2
Salvamentos para el as dominicano de los Marlins, Sandy Alcántara, quien además es el líder en entradas lanzadas en las Grandes Ligas (213.0). Desde que el rescate se convirtió en una estadística oficial en 1969, la única vez, según Elias, que un lanzador registró un salvamento en una campaña en la que lideró Grandes Ligas en entradas lanzadas fue cuando Phil Niekro lo hizo en 1978.
2
El número de equipos para los cuales Jo Adell ha conectado el cuadrangular más largo de la campaña. Dio un bambinazo de 449 pies para los Angelinos el 10 de mayo y luego, tras un cambio a mitad de año, conectó uno de 455 pies para los Guardianes el 18 de agosto. Ningún otro jugador en la Era Statcast ha dado el vuelacercas más largo de su club en múltiples equipos en la misma temporada.
3.98
La proporción de ponches por cada base por bolas del novato de los Guardianes, Parker Messick. Messick podría ser finalista al Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, gracias a un comando que es sumamente inusual para alguien con tan poca experiencia en Grandes Ligas. El único otro novato en la Era Moderna (desde 1900) con al menos 180 entradas y una mejor proporción K/BB fue el miembro del Salón de la Fama Don Sutton (4.02), con los Dodgers de 1966.
6.7
El bWAR (modelo de Victorias Sobre Reemplazo de Baseball-Reference) de la sensación novata de los Tigres, Kevin McGonigle. Es el más alto de todos los tiempos para un jugador en una temporada de debut en la que pasó la mayor parte del año con 21 años o menos. La marca anterior era de 6.6, conseguida tres veces: Por el dominicano Albert Pujols en el 2001, Frank Robinson en 1956 y aquel tal Ted Williams que mencionamos anteriormente, en 1939.
1.16
La efectividad de Cam Schlittler como visitante. Es la tercera mejor en la Era de la Pelota Viva para un lanzador con al menos 100 episodios fuera de casa. Las únicas mejores cifras pertenecieron a los miembros del Salón de la Fama Bob Gibson (0.81) en 1968 y Greg Maddux (1.12) en 1995. (Cabe destacar que ninguno estaba en su segunda temporada de Grandes Ligas en ese momento).
235
El EFE+ de Shohei Ohtani en 85.2 innings lanzados.
Es demasiado fácil acostumbrarse a lo que hace Ohtani e incluso restarle importancia a su campaña como jugador de dos vías, dado que los problemas de lesiones lo obligaron a dejar de lanzar a principios de julio. ¡Pero esto no es normal! En la Era Moderna, apenas otros ocho abridores de las Ligas Americana/Liga Nacional han registrado un EFE+ de al menos ese nivel con un mínimo de 85 entradas lanzadas:
Jacob deGrom, Mets de 2021: 373
Pedro Martínez, Medias Rojas de 2000: 291
Greg Maddux, Bravos de 1994: 271
Maddux, Bravos de 1995: 260
Bob Gibson, Cardenales de 1968: 258
Clayton Kershaw, Dodgers de 2016: 237
Clay Buchholz, Medias Rojas de 2013: 237
Obviamente, es inherentemente más impresionante registrar un EFE+ de ese nivel lanzando durante una temporada más completa. ¿Pero saben qué más es impresionante? Conseguir un EFE+ tan alto mientras también registras OPS de .902 en casi 600 visitas al plato.
De nuevo, no es normal. Ni siquiera para Ohtani.
47
La cifra de bases robadas, líder de las Mayores, del segunda base de los Nacionales, el dominicano Nasim Núñez, quien por lo demás está teniendo dificultades ofensivas esta temporada. Núñez tiene OPS de .529. El único otro jugador en la Era Moderna con OPS inferior a .550 que aun así logró robarse 40 bases fue Rollie Zeider (OPS de .548, 49 robos) de los Medias Blancas de 1910.
.374
El porcentaje de slugging de Cal Raleigh. El mismo Cal Raleigh que disparó 60 cuadrangulares la temporada pasada. De las nueve ocasiones anteriores en las que un jugador tuvo una campaña de 60 bambinazos, el porcentaje de slugging más bajo en la campaña siguiente había sido el .485 de Roger Maris en 1962. Eso sigue siendo más de 100 puntos superior al de Raleigh, quien pasó de ocupar el tercer lugar entre los bateadores calificados de MLB en SLG el año pasado (.589) a estar ahora entre los últimos 25.
42
Salvamentos desperdiciados por los Nacionales, un nuevo récord de Grandes Ligas. La marca anterior era de 36, establecida por los Medias Blancas en el 2024, cuando perdieron 121 juegos. Se podría decir que los Nacionales hicieron “volar” ese récord.
217, 28
Totales de ponches de los compañeros de los Filis Kyle Schwarber y el venezolano Luis Arráez, respectivamente. Schwarber está compitiendo por el liderato de ponches de MLB, mientras que Arráez (quien llegó procedente de los Gigantes en un cambio durante la Fecha Límite) terminará de último en ponches entre los bateadores calificados de la Gran Carpa.
Según Elias, sólo ha habido cuatro ocasiones en la Era de la Expansión (desde 1961) en las que el líder de MLB en ponches y el jugador con la menor cantidad de ponches (nuevamente, entre los bateadores calificados) terminaron la campaña en el mismo equipo… ¡y dos de ellas también involucraron a los Filis!
Medias Blancas de 1963: Dave Nicholson (más ponches), Nellie Fox (menos ponches)
Filis de 1965: Dick Allen (más), Octavio “Cookie” Rojas (menos)
Filis de 1976: Mike Schmidt (más), Dave Cash (menos)
Angelinos de 1982: Reggie Jackson (más), Tim Foli (menos)
0.8
Terminemos con la recta. Éste es el porcentaje de todos los pitcheos en MLB este año que han sido registrados a 100 mph o más. No se trata sólo de que sea el porcentaje más alto de la era de seguimiento de pitcheos (que se remonta al 2008), sino de que ni siquiera está cerca. ¡La cantidad de pitcheos de 100 mph o más ha aumentado en un 43.5%… tan sólo desde el año pasado!
Una razón más para que tengan nuestro permiso de ignorar a cualquier veterano que intente decirles que antes los lanzadores tiraban igual de duro.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Cam Schlittler is one start away from joining Ron Guidry in Yankees history
item.dc:creator: Tate Mosher
item.description: After his electric performance in Game 3 of the American League Wild Card series versus the Boston Red Sox last season, expectations for New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler suddenly grew for 2026. The 25-year-old was a seventh round selection in the 2022 draft by New York, but nonetheless rocketed through the minor leagues to make his debut in July 2025. Over that regular season, he made 14 starts with a 2.96 ERA. With the season he had plus that exceptional showing against Boston in a
item.content:encoded:
After his electric performance in Game 3 of the American League Wild Card series versus the Boston Red Sox last season, expectations for New York Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler suddenly grew for 2026.
The 25-year-old was a seventh round selection in the 2022 draft by New York, but nonetheless rocketed through the minor leagues to make his debut in July 2025. Over that regular season, he made 14 starts with a 2.96 ERA.
With the season he had plus that exceptional showing against Boston in a winner-take-all playoff game, anyone could have said he would be a good pitcher. However, Schlittler's performance this season has somehow blown expectations out of the water.
Potential Yankees history
Ahead of his 33rd and final start of the regular season Thursday versus the Tampa Bay Rays, the All-Star can make some franchise history. Per Gary Phillips of NY Daily News, Schlittler can become the third Yankee starting pitcher ever to finish a season with an ERA below 2.00.
Across 32 starts, Schlittler is 14-6 with a 1.94 ERA. He has pitched 190 ⅔ innings, striking out 234 and walking 47. He had a splendid half-season in 2025, but has impressively toned down the walks and upped the strikeouts this year.
With the way things look currently, Schlittler will win the AL Cy Young Award when it is announced in November. If so, he will become the seventh Yankee to win the award, and would join his teammate Gerrit Cole (2023) in the honor.
Looking ahead to the postseason
Aug 28, 2026; Bronx, New York, USA; New York Yankees pitcher Cam Schlittler (31) pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the first inning at Yankee Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Tom Horak-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
New York is locked into their current position of the No. 4 seed in the AL. They will host the No. 5 seed in the Wild Card round, with the winner advancing to take on the Rays in the Division Series starting Oct. 3.
In all likelihood, it will be a rematch of last year's Wild Card with the Red Sox traveling to the Bronx for a best-of-three. Including that series, Schlittler is 3-1 with a 0.56 ERA and 39 strikeouts against his hometown team in his brief career.
With the Massachusetts native taking the mound Thursday versus Tampa Bay, he likely will not pitch Game 1 against Boston next Tuesday. A normal rest schedule would have him in line for Wednesday's Game 2.

Pero el verdadero alcance de la noche va más allá de una carrera por el liderato de cuadrangulares. Rice acaba de entrar de lleno en l
item.content:encoded:
El número 41 apareció en la pantalla del Yankee Stadium y, por un instante, los Yankees volvieron a mirar hacia 1961.
Ben Rice conectó dos cuadrangulares el miércoles ante Tampa Bay para llegar a 41 en la temporada. El segundo puso al primera base de Nueva York en el mismo escalón de jonrones que Pete Alonso, Junior Caminero y Yordan Álvarez en la Liga Americana.
Pero el verdadero alcance de la noche va más allá de una carrera por el liderato de cuadrangulares. Rice acaba de entrar de lleno en la conversación por el MVP de la Liga Americana en la última semana del calendario. Sus números de temporada, después de 162 partidos para Nueva York, son 41 jonrones, 97 carreras anotadas, 148 hits, .263 de promedio, .362 de porcentaje de embasarse y .899 de OPS.
Al otro lado del clubhouse está Cam Schlittler.
El derecho de 25 años se convirtió en el brazo alrededor del cual gira la conversación por el Cy Young de la Americana. Después de 32 apariciones suma 14-6, 1.94 de ERA, 190.2 innings, 234 ponches y 0.91 de WHIP.
Pareja que entraría a los libros de historia de Yankees
Si Rice terminara conquistando el MVP y Schlittler el Cy Young, los Yankees volverían a tener en una misma temporada a los ganadores de los dos premios individuales más importantes de la Liga Americana. La última vez ocurrió en 1961.
Ninguno de los dos llegó a Nueva York con la etiqueta de fenómeno inevitable.
Rice fue elegido por los Yankees en la ronda 12 del Draft de 2021, con la selección 363, procedente de Dartmouth. Schlittler fue seleccionado en la séptima ronda de 2022, con el pick 220, después de jugar en Northeastern.
No fueron elecciones de primera ronda. No fueron nombres destinados desde el Draft a cargar con el uniforme de los Yankees.
Hoy, sin embargo, Rice es un bateador de 41 jonrones y Schlittler es el líder de una rotación que tiene al resto de la industria hablando del Cy Young. MLB describió recientemente la transformación de Schlittler como la de un séptima ronda convertido en All-Star y candidato al premio.
Y mientras Aaron Judge pasó buena parte de 2026 fuera por lesión, Rice terminó ocupando el espacio ofensivo que quedó abierto. Judge apenas disputó 66 encuentros y bateó .241 con 18 cuadrangulares.
¡Qué sucedió en 1961 para los Yankees!
Roger Maris y Whitey Ford escribieron una de las temporadas más reconocibles en la historia de la franquicia.
Maris bateó 61 cuadrangulares, rompió el récord de 60 que Babe Ruth había establecido en 1927 y terminó como MVP de la Liga Americana. En 161 partidos produjo .269/.372/.620, con 141 carreras impulsadas.
Ford, mientras tanto, tuvo una temporada que parecía diseñada para acompañar semejante hazaña: 25-4, 3.21 de ERA, 283 innings y 209 ponches. Ganó el Cy Young.
Los Yankees ganaron 109 juegos, conquistaron la Liga Americana por ocho juegos y después vencieron a Cincinnati en cinco partidos para ganar la Serie Mundial.
Existe además una precisión histórica importante. En 1961 todavía había un solo Cy Young para toda MLB. El premio comenzó a entregarse por separado en cada liga en 1967. Ford fue, por tanto, el ganador absoluto del Cy Young de 1961.
Rice no necesita batear 61 para entrar en esta conversación. Schlittler tampoco necesita reproducir exactamente los números de Ford.
Lo extraordinario sería que dos Yankees seleccionados fuera de las primeras rondas terminaran colocando sus nombres junto a Maris y Ford en la misma fotografía de premios.
¿Hay otros equipos con Cy Young y MVP en la misma temporada?
Antes de 1967, cuando el Cy Young era único para toda MLB, ocurrió con los Braves de 1957 —Hank Aaron y Warren Spahn—, White Sox de 1959 —Nellie Fox y Early Wynn—, Pirates de 1960 —Dick Groat y Vern Law— y Dodgers de 1962 —Maury Wills y Don Drysdale—.
Después de la división del premio por liga, la lista continuó con casos como Boston en 1986, Milwaukee en 1981, Oakland en 1990, Atlanta en 1991, Chicago White Sox en 1993, Oakland en 2002, St. Louis en 2005 y Minnesota en 2006. MLB registra 18 ocasiones en las que dos jugadores de un mismo equipo consiguieron MVP y Cy Young en la misma temporada hasta ese último caso.
También existe otra variante. Un mismo jugador ganó ambos premios en una temporada. Justin Verlander lo hizo en 2011, mientras Clayton Kershaw lo consiguió en 2014. En total, 11 pitchers han ganado Cy Young y MVP en el mismo año.
Por eso el último tramo de 2026 tiene una particularidad para Nueva York.
Today in 1961, Roger Maris of the @Yankees surpasses Babe Ruth’s record with his 61st homerun of the season. ⚾️
(📽 “61” released in 2001)#TodayInSports #PinstripePride
https://t.co/QJYClMw96G
Ben Rice y Cam Schlittler están en carrera por estos dos prestigiosos premios y también están intentando devolver a los Yankees a una fotografía que no aparece desde que Roger Maris y Whitey Ford hicieron historia hace 65 años.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees news: Could New York shut Clarke Schmidt down amid injury concern? appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
As the New York Yankees prepare for the playoffs, they are also trying to manage some of the injuries they're dealing with. One of those players is Clarke Schmidt, who has been working through a biceps injury. He's been going through testing, and though it seems like he's progressing, there's a chance that the Yankees consider shutting him down, according to MLB.com.
"Sept. 22 was a 'better' day for Schmidt, who felt discomfort while warming up Sept. 20 at Arizona. If Schmidt is unable to pitch Sept. 24, the Yankees may shut him down," MLB.com wrote.
That's not the best news for the Yankees, as Schmidt is an important part of the team. Especially with it being the playoffs, they want to be as healthy as possible. Right now those chances are looking slim, but it all depends on whether he's able to pitch in their final game of the series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
The Yankees are already going to be without Aaron Judge for their first playoff series as he deals with a calf injury. He is still hoping to come back at some point, but the goal is to be as healthy as possible.
"My goal is to come back as soon as I can," Judge said. "That's what we're doing right now. If [Boone] says I'm not gonna be ready, I've got no control over that. I've got control over what I can do to try to get back."
It'll be interesting to see what the Yankees' lineup looks like by the time they get to the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
On Thursday, the New York Yankees will finish their series with the Tampa Bay Rays in the Bronx.
They are coming off a 9-2 win on Wednesday.
Yankees Legend CC Sabathia Sends Out Heartfelt Post
This week, the Yankees will honor 2009 World Series Champion pitcher CC Sabathia.
They will retire his jersey.
Sabathia sent out a heartfelt post that had 15,000 likes.
He wrote (on September 23): “Damn I’m really getting my number retired at Monument Park this weekend 🥲”
Here’s what people were saying in the comments:
Gary Sheffield Jr.: “Congrats! And get A-Rod in the club as well.”
@Jronmar4: “I’m gonna be there for it! Can’t wait”
@cmols14: “Loved watching you toe the rubber in the Bronx much props”
@Da_Mon1027: “The best pitcher I ever got to see in person. Well deserved. Loved how as your speed declined your greatness never did, switching up your pitching style and succeeding is a story I use to motivate myself and others. You are the man.”
@NeverDive10: “As a season ticket holder for most of your Yankee career, it’s very believable. You deserve it. Congrats!”
@greg_broyles: “Well deserved by your amazing performances. Oh BTW, and you tossed my daughter a ball at a game in Atlanta….and yelled at a guy who tried to take it from her. You are class and forever loved.”
@SportsRJ: “Thank you CC for being awesome in Pinstripes! You deserve it! #RepBX”
@GabrielCay2: “One of the best I have ever seen, thank you”
Looking At Sabathia
Sabathia was picked in the 1st round of the 1998 MLB Draft.
He spent 19 seasons in the MLB with the Cleveland Guardians, Milwaukee Brewers (and Yankees).

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Projecting the Yankees' playoff bullpen trust tree behind Headrick, Blackburn, Bednar
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo
item.description: The New York Yankees have three main arms in their bullpen who they can rely on during the postseason. This trio of relievers consists of closer David Bednar, Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn, the Yankees' best relief assets all season. But who can they count on in the trust tree behind these three relief pitchers? Let's try to project which bullpen arms the Yankees can lean on in the playoffs from most to least trustworthy. Yankees' most trustworthy relievers as playoffs approach Yankees manag
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have three main arms in their bullpen who they can rely on during the postseason. This trio of relievers consists of closer David Bednar, Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn, the Yankees' best relief assets all season.
But who can they count on in the trust tree behind these three relief pitchers? Let's try to project which bullpen arms the Yankees can lean on in the playoffs from most to least trustworthy.
Yankees' most trustworthy relievers as playoffs approach
Yankees manager Aaron Boone has Bednar, Headrick and Blackburn, who he can go to in the late innings if the team has the lead or is in a tie game. But the Yankees are going to need more than that if they're going to make a deep run.
This is where Will Warren will likely come in as someone that can give the Yankees some key innings in long relief in the playoffs. Warren has not allowed a run in three innings as a reliever this season, and has pitched well as of late overall (2.45 ERA in September).
Hear me out on this next one: If Tim Hill makes the postseason roster, he will step up for the Yankees. Hill has allowed just one earned run across 11.1 playoff innings for the Yankees in the last two years. Since May 31, Hill has seen his ERA balloon from 2.53 to 4.71. But he is postseason tested, which means Boone and the Yankees should be able to count on him.
Last but not least, the sixth most trustworthy bullpen option could be newcomer John Schreiber. The right-hander has a 2.00 ERA over nine innings since joining the Yankees at the beginning of the month. Like Hill, Schreiber has postseason success, posting five scoreless relief appearances against the Yankees, ironically, in the 2024 postseason while pitching for the Kansas City Royals.
Who the Yankees shouldn't trust in ther playoff bullpen
Now we get to the part, where the names on this list probably should be pitching in lower leverage spots in the postseason. Fernando Cruz would've been included here, but his return is in doubt due to a partially torn UCL in his right elbow. Beyond Cruz, there is a pair of starters who are coming back from injury that likely can't be trusted at this point.
No. 1 is Clarke Schmidt, who just experienced biceps soreness when trying to warm up in the bullpen on Sunday. Schmidt came back from 2025 Tommy John surgery on September 16, but has been limited to one appearance, where he recorded two outs. It's hard to see how he could be high up on the trust tree in the postseason if the Yankees keep him on the playoff roster.
The second starter is Ryan Weathers, who had a breakout season for the Yankees this year. The expectation was that Weathers could be a solid relief option in the playoffs, but he is now unlikely to return in the regular season due to his left forearm flexor strain. It's difficult to envision Weathers coming back healthy at this point and being a trusted reliever in the biggest games of the year.
Should the Yankees choose to go: Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodón, Bednar, Headrick, Blackburn, Warren, Hill, Schreiber, Weathers, Schmidt, that would mean there's one more spot available for a pitcher on a 13-man staff. This last slot would come down to: Luis Gil, Michael Fulmer or Ryan Yarbrough.
While Gil has the most upside of the three, he can be erratic with his command at times. He also has a 6.75 ERA for his career in the postseason. Fulmer has a 4.50 ERA since joining the Yankees last month and Yarbrough is better suited to give length when the team is trailing. Whoever the Yankees decide to give the last spot to will be a low leverage option and at the bottom of the trust tree.

item.title: [The Big Lead] Ben Rice joins list of Yankee legends featuring Babe Ruth, Lou Gehrig & Joe DiMaggio
item.dc:creator: Matt Larter
item.description: The MLB season has seen Ben Rice etch his name alongside some of the greatest players in New York Yankees history. The 27-year-old slugger reached the 40-home run mark Wednesday during a 9-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays, putting him in an exclusive group of Yankees who have hit at least 40 home runs in a season at age 27 or younger. That list features legendary names including Babe Ruth, Lou Gehrig and Mickey Mantle, all of whom accomplished the feat twice. Joe DiMaggio, Roger Maris, Aaron Ju
item.content:encoded:
The MLB season has seen Ben Rice etch his name alongside some of the greatest players in New York Yankees history.
The 27-year-old slugger reached the 40-home run mark Wednesday during a 9-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays, putting him in an exclusive group of Yankees who have hit at least 40 home runs in a season at age 27 or younger.
That list features legendary names including Babe Ruth, Lou Gehrig and Mickey Mantle, all of whom accomplished the feat twice. Joe DiMaggio, Roger Maris, Aaron Judge and Juan Soto are also members of the group.
MORE: Blue Jays & Mariners make MLB history in worst way
Rice powers his way into Yankees history
Rice did not stop at one home run Wednesday, launching two against the Rays to reach 41 for the season. Through 151 games, he is batting .263 with 41 home runs and 97 RBI.
His power has been a major part of an impressive season, and reaching 40 home runs places Rice in company with some of the most celebrated sluggers to ever wear the Yankees uniform.
While Rice has already secured his place in the team’s statistical history, the Yankees are now preparing for the postseason.
Yankees prepare for the postseason
New York has clinched the American League’s top Wild Card position, holding a 10-game advantage over the Chicago White Sox, who occupy the final Wild Card spot. However, the Yankees will not be able to catch Tampa Bay for the AL East title.
The Yankees enter the final stretch of the regular season five games behind the Rays with only four games remaining. That leaves New York focused on preparing for the postseason rather than chasing the division crown.
The Yankees will send ace Cam Schlittler to the mound Thursday for the series finale against Tampa Bay. They will then close out the regular season with a three-game series against the Baltimore Orioles over the weekend.
For Rice, the final games offer an opportunity to build on a milestone season. At just 27 years old, his 40-home run campaign has already placed him alongside an extraordinary collection of Yankees legends, giving him a notable piece of franchise history heading into the postseason.

item.content:encoded:
Knicks Superfans Wanted for a Paid Commercial in New York
Remember When The New York Knicks Won the NBA Finals?
New York sports fans are having a tough go at it this fall.
The New York Mets are struggling to say the least. An Aaron Judge injury could affect the New York Yankees in the playoff season.
After beating the Dallas Cowboys at home, during the 1st game of the season, the New York Giants were dealt a devastating blow. QB1 Jaxson Dart is out for the season.
In times like these we like to dive back into happier times, like when the New York Knick won the NBA Finals beating the San Antonio Spurs back in June of 2026.
Who could forget Jalen Brunson and the boys coming back from behind every game to take the championship in 5 games?
I still dream about OG tipping the ball in during Game 4. Incredible run.
At least we have the Knicks (and the Bills if you're into that).
With that being said, New York Knick fans...you're needed!
New York Knick Fans Needed for Paid Commercial
Are you a New York Knick super fan? If so, you're needed!
House of Talent put out a casting call looking for a very specific fan group. They write on their website "Seeking massive Knicks Superfans in New York City for a paid commercial for a tech brand."
There is no previous acting experience needed and they add:
We're looking for friends, families, firefighters, nurses, and people engaged with & servicing their community.
It's a paid gig too! Those picked to be in the commercial will be paid $750 for 10 hours. Pretty sweet deal if you ask me.
If You Want to Be in the Knicks Commercial Here's What To Do
So you want to be in the commercial? Here's what you need to do.
Fill out the application on their website knicksfans.castingcrane.com. The applications must be in by September 25th, 2026.
Callbacks will be on Zoom on September 30th.
You also must be available for a fitting on October 5th, and filming on October 6th and 7th.
According to the website, the commercial will be used for the following:
All Media (including industry events such as Meta Connect, Cannes, CES, AdWeek etc. and any events attended by or sponsored by advertisers, etc).
Let us know if you get the job and we'll keep an eye out for ya!

item.dc:creator: Justin Terranova
item.description: It’s been an exciting September for Austin Wells off the field — and the Yankees hope there will be a thrilling October on it to match. The Yankees catcher got engaged to girlfriend Caroline Nielson earlier this month, according to photos she shared of the proposal on Instagram. Nielson posted Wednesday photos of a touching beach scene with Wells down on one knee before the couple embraces. The “forever and ever” caption suggests that the proposal took place Sept. 3 — an off day for the Yankees
item.content:encoded:
It’s been an exciting September for Austin Wells off the field — and the Yankees hope there will be a thrilling October on it to match.
The Yankees catcher got engaged to girlfriend Caroline Nielson earlier this month, according to photos she shared of the proposal on Instagram.
Nielson posted Wednesday photos of a touching beach scene with Wells down on one knee before the couple embraces.
The “forever and ever” caption suggests that the proposal took place Sept. 3 — an off day for the Yankees between series in California against the Angels and Padres.
They also included a photo of their daughter, Lucy, as part of the joyous moment.
Several significant others of Yankees teammates were quick to toast the couple in the comments section.
“My heart!!!!! Let’s get these two married!!! 🥹🥹🥹♥️♥️♥️♥️” wrote Ava O’Connor, who is dating outfielder Spencer Jones.
“The best off day in the history of off days,” wrote Carlos Rodon’s wife, Ashley.
“SCREAMING CRYING,” wrote Ben Rice’s girlfriend, Sara Falkson.
It is unclear when the couple first started dating. They announced that Nielson was expecting a child last November in one of the first public signs of a relationship.
Before the big day, Wells has an important postseason in front of him.
The 27-year-old catcher has somewhat rebounded from a miserable start to the season, pushing his average up to .185 after dipping down to .150 in July.
Wells, who is respected by the Yankees for his skills behind the plate, will likely be a mainstay in the lineup during the postseason.
Shop Yankees Merch
That will begin next week when the Yankees in all likelihood will take on the Red Sox in a best-of-three wild card series in The Bronx.
Wells did have perhaps his biggest moment in pinstripes when the rivals met last season in the same round, driving home the game-winning run with an eighth-inning single in Game 2.
The Yankees evened the series that night and went on to win Game 3 the following evening.
Now, Wells and the Yankees will look for an even deeper postseason run with Nielson no doubt cheering him on from the stands.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge said he wants to return for next week’s wild-card series. Until he does come back, the slugger and the rest of the New York Yankees will be curious to see if slugger Ben Rice can homer again.
With four games remaining, Rice is among seven MLB players with at least 40 home runs, and he will attempt to continue his late-season surge Thursday night when New York hosts the Tampa Bay Rays, the American League East champion.
The Yankees (91-67) are assured of hosting the wild-card series and probably will face the Boston Red Sox for the second straight year. New York might be without Judge, who is dealing with a strained right calf after playing in seven games following being out with a fractured right rib.
On Monday, manager Aaron Boone described Judge’s strain as moderate and indicated he was not necessarily expecting the three-time American League MVP to be available. After the Yankees improved to 50-42 in games Judge has missed with Wednesday’s 9-2 rout of the Rays, the eight-time All-Star expressed confidence in his ability to return by next week.
“My goal is to come back as soon as I can,” Judge said. “If you ask me if I’m going to be back, I’m gonna tell you, yeah, I’m doing everything I can every single day I show up here to get back and be ready to go.”
Judge expressed confidence in his return after watching Rice hit a pair of solo homers on Wednesday, giving him 41 home runs in his second full season. Rice had three hits and a walk and is batting .349 with five homers in his past 12 games and .333 with seven homers and 17 RBIs in his past 27.
For the season, he is batting .263 with 97 RBIs after finishing with 26 homers, 65 RBIs and a .255 batting average last year.
“Each year, he’s gotten better,” Judge said of the 27-year-old. “Each month he’s gotten better. Even through bad slumps, he’s just making the reads and making the changes he needs to get back to his normal self. So it’s been fun to watch. He’s a complete player.”
Rice is hitting .381 against the Rays (96-62), who clinched the AL East with a 6-1 win over the Yankees on Tuesday night. After clinching, the Rays on Wednesday sat Yandy Diaz, who had a pair of two-run singles in the clincher.
Junior Caminero will be in the lineup to keep his streak of playing each game going but likely will be replaced after a few at-bats. Caminero took two at-bats and was lifted for a pinch hitter in the sixth.
“I just want to see good health and some guys freshened up,” Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said. “It’s been a long season. They’ve played really hard to get to this point. Let’s find a way to continue to get our work in, and I know and trust that whoever’s on that field, they’re going to do everything they can to win games.”
Whoever is in the lineup for the Rays will face right-hander Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.94 ERA), who will make his final regular-season start before likely starting Game 1 of the wild-card series.
Since lasting 4 1/3 innings in an 8-2 loss to the Los Angeles Dodgers on July 19, Schlittler is 5-0 with a 1.46 ERA in his past 11 starts. The Yankees fell to 20-12 in his starts on Saturday when he allowed one earned run on three hits in six innings in a no-decision during a 5-3 loss at Arizona.
Schlittler is 1-2 with a 2.63 ERA in four career starts against the Rays.
Left-hander Ian Seymour (9-7, 4.38 ERA) originally was slated to start Wednesday but had his start pushed back a day to give Freddy Peralta extra rest to face Philadelphia on Friday.
Seymour is 0-1 with a 5.79 ERA in three starts this month, including Friday’s 4-2 loss to Boston when he allowed four runs on seven hits in five innings. One of his best starts this season occurred July 7 in Tampa Bay when he struck out 12 in 5 1/3 innings during a 6-4 win over the Yankees.
-Field Level Media

item.title: [rumbunter.com] Jazz Chisholm Jr.'s middling Yankees walk year could cost Pirates in Brandon Lowe chase
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: Pretty much since the moment he took his first at-bats in a Pittsburgh Pirates uniform, there's been incessant clamoring for Brandon Lowe to get a long-term extension. There are certainly concerns about handing big money to a 32-year-old middle infielder, but everything Lowe has shown us this season suggests he's worthy of a massive investment. Of course, the Bucs haven't gone that route yet, and we don't even know if they've breached the topic with their star slugger. We know he's interested in
item.content:encoded:
Pretty much since the moment he took his first at-bats in a Pittsburgh Pirates uniform, there's been incessant clamoring for Brandon Lowe to get a long-term extension. There are certainly concerns about handing big money to a 32-year-old middle infielder, but everything Lowe has shown us this season suggests he's worthy of a massive investment.
Of course, the Bucs haven't gone that route yet, and we don't even know if they've breached the topic with their star slugger. We know he's interested in sticking around, but to this point, the Pirates haven't made it clear if they're willing to spend the kind of money it'll take to keep him in Pittsburgh.
That hesitancy might wind up costing them in the near future if it lasts. A thin free-agent market for bats -- especially when it comes to infielders -- is going to drive Lowe's price tag up, especially since a lot of his direct competition hasn't performed at their peak levels in 2026.
Lack of infield competition in free agency could push Brandon Lowe's price tag beyond Pirates' range
The main story here is that Lowe has played his way into "star free agent" territory. The two-time All-Star (who should have earned a third trip to the Midsummer Classic) is hitting .260/.330/.489 with a 119 wRC+ this season, hitting more than 30 home runs for the second consecutive season. He leads all second baseman this year in homers and slugging percentage.
He's also added elite defense to his repertoire this year (+14 Defensive Runs Saved and +14 Outs Above Average), which has helped him achieve a career-best fWAR of 4.7. With a strong final week, he could join Brice Turang as the only second basemen in the league to cross the 5.0 threshold.
Beyond that, though, it's going to help his free-agent case that some of the other star infielders aren't putting up big contract years. Jazz Chisholm Jr. is the obvious point of comparison as a fellow second baseman; he's had a respectable season (19 homers, 40 steals, 3.4 fWAR), but his OPS has dropped by nearly 100 points from his Silver-Slugging-winning effort a year ago. He, like Bo Bichette (95 wRC+), has probably cost himself a few dollars this season.
In other words, there's a really good case to be made that, save for Teruaki Sato of Nippon Professional Baseball, Lowe will be the best infielder to hit free agency this offseason. There's also going to be competition in the form of Luis Arraez (111 wRC+, 4.2 fWAR) and Jake Bauers (147 wRC+, 3.7 fWAR), but the former is a contact-first hitter and Bauers is a first baseman. The combination of power and defensive value that Lowe offers are unparalleled in this class.
You can be sure other teams know that and will offer contracts that reflect such a fact. You can also be sure that the Pirates probably won't match the the highest offer Lowe is likely to receive. As such, if he's going to remain with the team beyond 2026, a last-second extension is probably our final hope.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees' Aaron Judge Expresses Displeasure With Aaron Boone's Description Of Injury

Manager Aaron Boone has said the team does not plan to use Judge in the Wild Card Series, but he has not ruled him out. Boone described Judge's calf strain as "moderate" on Tuesday, but Judge is not a fan of him saying that. "I don't know why he used those words," Judge told reporters on Wednesday. Despite details of his injury that are known to the public, Judge is say
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees start the postseason on Tuesday, and three-time MVP Aaron Judge is on the injured list with a calf strain.
Manager Aaron Boone has said the team does not plan to use Judge in the Wild Card Series, but he has not ruled him out. Boone described Judge's calf strain as "moderate" on Tuesday, but Judge is not a fan of him saying that.
"I don't know why he used those words," Judge told reporters on Wednesday.
Despite details of his injury that are known to the public, Judge is saying he plans to be ready for Game 1 of the Wild Card Series. He received a PPP injection on Monday and is working hard to get back in the lineup for the Yankees' first postseason series.
"Everybody's 'moderate' is a little different," Judge said. "I think your moderate is a little different than my moderate."
Whether or not Judge comes back remains to be seen, but as of right now, it does not seem like his manager is expecting him to play when the Yankees begin their quest for a World Series. Still, Judge knows that what Boone says does not impact how hard he works to return.
"Boonie is my guy. I've always got his back," Judge said. "I know he makes the right decisions. Obviously, as a player you don't want to hear that, but that's out of my control. I've got to come back and be ready to go, and that's what I'm focused on right now."

item.content:encoded:
With less than a week until the 2026 MLB playoffs begin, our baseball insiders have been cultivating their sources and are ready to break down the questions, teams and themes that will shape October -- even before the final 12-team postseason field is set.
What is the boldest take we’ve heard from an MLB exec? Is a Los Angeles Dodgers three-peat coming? Can the New York Yankees make a deep run -- with or without Aaron Judge? And who are the sleeper teams and under-the-radar players to watch?
Here’s the latest intel our MLB experts are hearing as Jeff Passan, Buster Olney, Jesse Rogers, Jorge Castillo and Alden Gonzalez empty their notebooks heading into the playoffs.
What is the boldest prediction you’ve heard from an MLB exec or scout?
Olney: The Padres are going to win the World Series for the first time in their history, with just about everything trending in the right direction. “Once you get into the postseason with all of the built-in off days, that’s going to help their bullpen -- which is the best,” he noted. The Padres’ starting pitching is the team’s biggest concern, but as the Dodgers demonstrated in 2024, you can win with three or four functional starters who are backed by a deep bullpen.
Passan: The Red Sox might be the No. 5 seed, but they’re going to win the American League pennant. Since the All-Star break, one evaluator pointed out, the Red Sox have the best offense in the AL. They’re also an MLB best in Fielding Independent Pitching, a predictive metric that suggests they will continue to throw well. It’s a deep bullpen. It’s a solid-enough rotation. It’s a productive lineup. And, perhaps most helpful of all, it’s the AL, where the path to the World Series is a sandy beach compared to the jungle of the National League.
Do MLB insiders think the Dodgers will turn it on in October again like they did the past two postseasons?
Gonzalez: The general sentiment about the Dodgers seems to be this: They’ll be the favorites until proven otherwise. That’s what they’ve elevated to. They’re too talented, too deep, and they’ve become too adept at navigating seasons to have many detractors, regardless of whatever adversity they might face.
These past couple of weeks have offered a perfect snapshot. The Dodgers’ offense was a serious concern, but now -- with Mookie Betts, Teoscar Hernandez and Kyle Tucker on a heater, and Shohei Ohtani back -- not so much. Their bullpen was, too, but Edwin Diaz has looked sharp since coming back, Roki Sasaki could once again become a weapon and Emmet Sheehan might be too. Regardless, their rotation is widely expected to be an equalizer.
Passan: They’re still the favorites, which is saying something when considering the fatigue that often attaches itself to dynastic teams. But the Dodgers have shown enough vulnerabilities that a number of evaluators believe another team will represent the NL in the World Series. One GM’s sentiment -- “I’d take every NL playoff team over every AL playoff team,” he said -- speaks to the sort of competition the Dodgers will face.
And with so many question marks about how Ohtani and Andy Pages and Blake Snell will fare after returning on the eve of the postseason with no rehab assignments, the Dodgers are not nearly the sure thing they’ve been in recent postseasons. At the same time, they remain, top to bottom, the most talented team in the game, and nobody would be surprised if they win their third consecutive World Series.
How much faith does the industry have in the Rays and Brewers turning the best regular-season records into World Series appearances?
Olney: There is more faith in the Brewers than I’ve ever heard, because the general perception is that they are just a better, deeper team than the group that was bulldozed by the Dodgers in last year’s postseason -- and they’ve got the best starting pitcher, in Jacob Misiorowski. “I think he might hit 107 [mph] in the playoffs,” speculated one evaluator, assessing the impact of the adrenaline, expectations and Misiorowski’s heightened competitiveness. And generally, there is a lot of respect for the Rays, particularly when measured against the low bar of the American League.
Rogers: As much as ever. The Brewers have more believers this year than last simply based on the top of their rotation led by Misiorowski and Logan Henderson. Their depth there is better as well. Robert Gasser has come on strong while rubber-armed Aaron Ashby is a key bullpen guy to go along with Abner Uribe and Trevor Megill.
On the Rays side, their draw for the postseason isn’t perfect -- according to one insider -- but if the Yankees and Red Sox play three games in the wild-card round, it’ll set things up nicely for them in the division series. After that, they’ll be heavy favorites to get to the Fall Classic.
Given Aaron Judge’s health questions, do those in the game think the Yankees will make another deep October run?
Castillo: Opinions vary around the majors. One front office executive said the Yankees have “no chance” of making a World Series run without Judge. Another said he believes it’s possible behind the pitching staff, though the executive added that the bullpen is seemingly running on fumes down the stretch.
Anything can happen in a three-game series. The Red Sox nearly bounced New York last year, falling short in Game 3 thanks to Cam Schlittler’s sterling performance.
After that, the Rays are reminiscent of the Blue Jays club that gave the Yankees trouble last year -- from the regular season through eliminating them in four games in the ALDS. Not having Judge undoubtedly hurts the Yankees’ chances of surviving the gauntlet.
Olney: It wouldn’t be a surprise if they emerge in the American League -- and nor would it be a surprise if they got knocked out in the first round. Without Judge, they are vulnerable against left-handed pitching, and Boston is loaded with lefties.
If they do survive the Red Sox, then they’ll open the division series on the road in the Trop, where they don’t match up well; the Rays’ style of play on their home surface caused all kinds of problems for the Yankees this year.
That all said, the Yankees have the best pitching of the AL teams; they have a good lineup (albeit not great); and their defense has improved.
Who else do MLB insiders feel could be this October’s most dangerous teams?
Rogers: As easy as it would be to pick an AL team to make a surprising run simply because the draw there is softer, experts like the Padres as a dangerous lower-seeded team. They have a good playoff formula now that the rotation has some help and the lineup is hitting for power. In fact, San Diego leads MLB in home runs in September. And of course, they have that vaunted bullpen.
With Aaron Judge on the shelf, the Red Sox are becoming a favorite pick among experts in the AL. Others point to Yankees pitching as their key to advancing. It’s really good behind Cy Young fave Cam Schlittler.
Gonzalez: The Phillies are often a popular pick for this question, and this year it’s no different. They have obvious flaws, from the makeup of their bullpen to their overall defense to, mostly, the status of Jesus Luzardo. But they have a bevy of top-shelf stars, the type that tend to make a major impact on October. They have the experience of having navigated these stakes as a group many times. They have a raucous home environment, one that arguably trumps any in the sport. And, lately, they have Aaron Nola looking like his vintage self.
Still: it’s hard to dismiss the Luzardo factor in all this. He changes everything. “If he’s healthy,” a rival front office executive said, “they’re my answer.” If not, he added, the Brewers are the better, more well-rounded team. Luzardo is that important.
Who are some under-the-radar players with industry buzz as potential postseason stars?
Castillo: Rays outfielder Victor Mesa Jr., Brewers first baseman Jake Bauers and Padres first baseman Ty France. Mesa, dumped in a trade by the Marlins in February, surfaced from Triple-A in late May to join Junior Caminero, Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda as dangerous bats. Bauers and France are veterans who lead their respective teams in wRC+ this season -- indicating, at least by that measure, that they’ve been the best hitters on their clubs -- and have been overshadowed.
Passan: In an era when the average fastball is 94.6 mph and pitchers throw it around 30% of the time, Cleveland left-hander Parker Messick and Milwaukee right-hander Logan Henderson are anomalies.
Messick, 25, is a favorite of scouts. He throws a four-seamer that averages 94 mph more than 40% of the time, and despite the relative lack of velocity, it’s been a banger of a pitch, the third-most-valuable heater in MLB behind Jacob Misiorowski’s and Cam Schlittler’s.
Henderson leans even more heavily on his fastball (45.7%) even though it’s slower (93.1 mph) and it has the sixth-highest run value.
Why do they work so well? Messick and Henderson both have exceptional control, and as much as velo rules the modern game, there is still room for pitching artistry, and they personify it.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Yankees' Ben Rice inspired by manager Aaron Boone's prediction to hit homers 40, 41
item.dc:creator: Alex Butler

item.content:encoded:
Sept. 24 (UPI) -- New York Yankees designated hitter Ben Rice said he was inspired by manager Aaron Boone to reach the 40 home run milestone during the 2026 season.
Rice told the reporters about the inspiration after he hit Nos. 40 and 41 in a 9-2 triumph over the Tampa Bay Rays on Wednesday in New York. He pointed at Boone after he hit the first pitch of the bottom of the first to right field for a 379-foot solo shot, emphasizing the manager-induced drive.
"I think I said, 'hey, that's 40 for you, Skip,'" Rice said on the Prime Video broadcast. "I told him 'thank you so much for inspiring me to get to 40.'"
Boone predicted at spring training that Rice would reach 39 home runs in 2026. Rice told reporters Wednesday that he didn't really go into the campaign with a certain total in mind, but honed in on the 40 mark once he drew close over the final stretch of the season.
"It's a cool milestone," Rice said. "It's not something you go into the season really aiming for. You don't really know how it's going to go. But as I was approaching that number, it was definitely something I was hoping to achieve."
Yankees third baseman Ryan McMahon doubled the lead with an RBI single in the second inning. Shortstop George Lombardi Jr. raked a 384-foot solo homer in the third. McMahon, who went 2 for 4, hit a grand slam later in the inning for a 7-0 Yankees lead.
Rays right fielder Jonny DeLuca responded with an RBI double in the top of the fourth. Rice followed with a 383-foot solo shot to lead off the bottom of that frame.
Center fielder Cedric Mullins hit a 375-foot solo homer in the top of the fifth for the Rays' final run. Yankees right fielder Heliot Ramos plated the game's last score with a sacrifice fly in the eighth.
Rice went 3 for 4 with two RBIs, two runs scored and a walk. He hit .263, with 23 doubles, four triples and 97 RBIs, in addition to his American League-leading 41 homers, through 151 games this season.
"I was confident he was going to have a really big year," Boone said, when asked about Rice at his postgame news conference.
"I probably wanted to make sure it was just south of a [home run total] number, maybe to maybe let him know that."
Yankees starter Gerrit Cole allowed three hits and two runs over 5 and 2/3 innings to improve to 10-9 this season. Rays starter Mason Englert allowed nine hits and eight runs over 3 and 2/3 innings to drop to 0-4.
The Yankees (91-67) will host the Rays (96-62) in a series finale at 7:05 p.m. EDT Thursday in New York. They will start their final series of the season -- against the Baltimore Orioles -- on Friday at Yankee Stadium.

item.title: [yanksgoyard.com] 3 surprising players who could crash Yankees' playoff roster in Wild Card round
item.dc:creator: Matthew Swigonski

item.content:encoded:
Despite their best efforts, the New York Yankees are all but guaranteed to face the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card Series. Like any time the two heated rivals face off against each other, the three-game set will almost certainly push both teams to do whatever it takes to gain an advantage. For the Yankees, that could mean adding a few surprising players on the roster that you might not expect.
With the Yankees nearly a lock to play the Red Sox, manager Aaron Boone has already been eyeing his likely starting rotation in preparation for the postseason. The Yankees will likely roll with a combination of Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, and Gerrit Cole. That rotation would likely lead to some creativity when it comes to how the rest of the roster is constructed.
That creativity could potentially be used exclusively within the team’s bullpen. Would that mean that Carlos Rodón is left off the roster for the short series in favor of a pitcher more capable of coming out of the pen? With plenty of tough innings between the Yankees and Red Sox coming up, there could be some surprise arms out of the bullpen to bridge the gap between the starters and closer David Bednar.
3 surprise pitchers who could give the Yankees valuable innings in the postseason
Over the last few weeks of the season, relievers Brent Headrick and Paul Blackburn have seemed to be feeling the effects of a long season where they have each thrown more than 77 innings. With that wear and tear weighing on their shoulders, they have both looked a little more human as of late. That doesn’t mean that they won’t step up when it matters the most in the postseason, but they may need some help.
The Yankees will need to collect at least 54 outs against the Red Sox in order to move on to the Divisional round. When it comes to the postseason, it doesn’t matter how you get those outs. In fact, it doesn’t even matter who gets those outs for you. For the Yankees, they could be giving the ball to a few pitchers that may turn some heads.
Ryan Weathers
While his battle with a nagging elbow flexor strain could complicate things, Ryan Weathers has the potential to become a game-changing pitcher for the Yankees in the Wild Card round. Out since August, Weathers may not come back in time to finish out the regular season. With the Yankees’ first postseason game scheduled for September 29, that doesn’t leave a lot of time for Weathers to make it back for a matchup against the Red Sox, either.
But if he can bounce back and throw an inning or two, Weathers may become one of the team’s most valuable weapons out of the pen. With a 9.4 K/9 rate this season, the southpaw is more than capable of picking up a much-needed punchout to quell a potential rally. Perhaps more importantly, he’s induced nine ground ball double plays in high-leverage situations this season.
If healthy enough to pitch, Weathers could be an effective option for Boone. That would go a long way toward saving relievers like Headrick and Blackburn for the later innings if needed.
Yerry de los Santos
With only three games to worry about in the Wild Card round, Boone could easily look to add as many versatile relievers as possible. Yerry de los Santos may not be the first name you'd think of when considering a lockdown postseason bullpen, but he could become a valuable arm against the Red Sox.
His propensity to fill the base paths with runners isn't exactly the best formula for postseason success. With a career WHIP of 1.334, it would be very unlikely that Boone would turn to de los Santos in a close game. But in the event of a blowout in either of the first two games, de los Santos would become the best option to eat innings and save the high-leverage arms for the next day. That could be invaluable in the long run.
With a high ground ball rate and an ability to miss barrels, de los Santos has been good at limiting the damage during his time with the Yankees. That could continue against the Red Sox. Just don't expect to see him jogging in from the bullpen in a tight one (even though he was briefly RP4, almost by default, in mid-August).
Elmer Rodriguez
After looking like a whole new pitcher following his most recent call up in August, Elmer Rodriguez offered fans a glimpse into his future as a postseason starter. Maybe just not this year, though. But that doesn't mean he won't be a big factor in the Wild Card round.
With an impressive combination of a power sinker and a four-seamer, Rodriguez is capable of getting ahead of hitters and establishing his fastball. This could allow him to set up his strong offering of breaking balls. On the season, batters are slugging just .182 off the sweeper and an embarrassingly low .091 off of his curveball.
As a short relief option, Rodriguez could see an uptick in velocity that would better play off of his breaking balls. With wipeout stuff, Rodriguez could be yet another surprise weapon for Boone to unleash out of the bullpen.

item.title: [nydailynews.com] No Yankees starter has had a better season than Ron Guidry. He marvels at Cam Schlittler
item.dc:creator: Gary Phillips

item.content:encoded:
Clad in a black tux and a matching bowtie, Ron Guidry stepped to the podium at the New York Hilton Midtown on Jan. 27, 2024 to recognize a fellow Yankee and to pass a torch.
Speaking at the Baseball Writers’ Association of America Awards Dinner in his Louisiana drawl, “Gator” introduced Gerrit Cole, voted the American League’s Cy Young for 2023. Guidry won the same award while wearing pinstripes back in 1978, and so he leapt at the BBWAA’s invitation to present Cole with the prestigious hardware.
Cole called it a “really special” moment with an “integral part of the organization,” as Guidry took him under his wing after he signed with the Yankees before the 2020 season.
“They called and asked, and I said, ‘Sure, I’d be honored to go give it to him,’” Guidry recently told the Daily News. “And it would be nice if Cam would do the same thing with Gerrit.”
By “Cam,” Guidry meant Cam Schlittler, who is poised to become the seventh Yankee to win the Cy Young and the first since Cole. The 25-year-old has been so stellar that Aaron Boone recently lobbied for the MVP Award, though Schlittler isn’t seen as a frontrunner for that trophy.
“He’s a stud,” the manager said.
With Schlittler set to make his 33rd and final regular season start against the Rays on Thursday, the right-hander is 14-6 with an American League-leading 1.94 ERA and 234 strikeouts over 190.2 innings. In just his first full big league season, he has put together one of the best campaigns by a Yankees starter in franchise history.
Guidry’s 1978 season is widely considered the best. No one is going to match his 25-3 record, nine shutouts or 273.2 innings that year, not with the way the sport has changed.
“Just a different game of baseball back then. It’s just not the same as it is now,” Schlittler said. “No one’s throwing that many innings. So he’s a legend for a reason.”
“He’s going to have to play hell to try to break my shutout record,” Guidry added with a laugh.
With a 1.74 ERA in 1978, Guidry is one of just two Yankees starters who have logged at least 30 starts and finished a season with a sub-2.00 ERA since earned runs became an official stat. Spud Chandler, who had a 1.64 ERA in 1943, is the other. Schlittler is trying to become the third.
Guidry also struck out 248 batters in 1978, a Yankees record at the time. Cole toppled him with 257 punchies in 2022.
An ace long before analytics became commonplace in baseball, Guidry also had a 9.1 fWAR in 1978, a record for Yankees pitchers. His 2.19 FIP ranks fifth behind a few guys who pitched in the early 1900s.
Like some of Guidry’s surface numbers, those stats easily outpace Schlittler’s still-sensational production; he leads all AL starters with a 6.1 fWAR. His 2.57 FIP that ranks second.
Regardless, Guidry is delighted that their names keep getting mentioned side by side.
“It’s always a compliment when somebody today is compared to somebody from yesterday,” the 76-year-old said. “It just so happens if you’re talking about Cam, you’re talking to me.
“That’s a compliment to me.”
Schlittler and Guidry haven’t gotten to know each other too well, but they have crossed paths since the former started showing up to big league camp two springs ago. Guidry is a frequent guest instructor, watching bullpens, parting his wisdom, and answering any questions the pinstripers’ new generation of pitchers may have.
Even two springs ago, months before Schlittler debuted, Guidry saw the makings of a future ace.
“You could see that there’s something there,” Guidry said.
Since then, Schlittler has bulked up, increased his velocity, cemented himself in Yankees postseason lore, and turned into the nastiest pitcher in a rotation that also features Cole, Max Fried and Carlos Rodón.
He’s also established himself as a rather competitive individual, whether it be between the lines or while beefing with rival fans on social media.
“He’s got that air about him. That, ‘I’m good, come get me,’” said Guidry, who has watched Schlittler quite a bit this year. “You’ve shown them that you have the stuff and you’re not afraid to throw it.”
The stuff Guidry mentioned is typically coming in hot.
With a four-seamer, a cutter and a sinker, Schlittler throws some variation of a fastball roughly 90% of the time, making his rise all the more impressive and unique. His four-seamer, meanwhile, averaged 98 mph entering Thursday’s game.
“You marvel at his fastball because he throws in excess of 100 miles per hour. Well, when you can throw that hard, you have a big advantage over a lot of hitters,” Guidry said, though he would like to see Schlittler develop some secondary stuff as he advances in his career.
Schlittler throws a curveball that grades out rather well, but he’s thrown it less than 10% of the time. He has also thrown a slider and previously toyed with a changeup and a splitter.
“At some point in his career, he’s going to have to start looking at something else to complement that because he’s not going to be able to stand up to the strain of throwing that hard for 20 years,” Guidry continued. “It might be 10 years, but it’s not going to be for 20 years. Even Nolan [Ryan] slowed up to 98 when he was 40 years old.”
While Guidry fired with his left arm during an entirely different era, he said that his prime self and Schlittler are “basically the same.” He noted that “we’re considered power pitchers” — though Guidry relied heavily on a fastball-slider combo — and that his Cy Young season was his first as a full-time starter in the majors.
Guidry began 1977 in the bullpen but began his run as a rotation staple by mid-May that year.
Now Guidry would like to see Schlittler join him on the short list of Yankees pitchers who have won the award.
“Any time a Yankee is in that position, you’re pulling for him,” Guidry said. “Because it don’t happen often.”

item.title: [Bozeman Daily Chronicle] Ben Rice tops Aaron Boone's preseason prediction of 39 homers, hitting 40th and then 41st
item.dc:creator: RONALD BLUM

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Ben Rice one-upped Aaron Boone. And then he two-upped the New York Yankees manager.
Boone predicted during spring training that Rice would finish with 39 home runs this season. Rice hit Nos. 40 and 41 in Wednesday night's 9-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays, tying for the American League home run lead.
He smiled and pointed at Boone when he returned to the dugout after driving Mason Englert's first pitch of the game into Yankee Stadium's right field second deck. Rice grinned at Boone some more after another solo homer in the fourth.
“I think I said, `Hey, there’s 40 for you,'” Rice recalled. “I was joking with him after the 41st one, saying, `Hey thanks for inspiring me this year.' But it’s all in good fun. Back in spring when he told me that, I knew that secretly meant he was hoping I’d hit 40.”
Rice is tied for the AL home run lead with Baltimore’s Pete Alonso, the Rays’ Junior Caminero and Houston’s Yordan Alvarez. He is hitting .263 and leads the Yankees with 97 RBIs and an .899 OPS, becoming a first-time All-Star and the biggest cog in an offense missing Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton for most of the season.
Boone deliberately picked an odd total rather than a round figure.
“I was confident he was going to have a really big year,” he said. “Probably wanted to make sure it was just south of a number, maybe to maybe let him know that.”
Rice, who had three hits and a walk, became the 13th Yankees player with a 40-home run season but just the third to reach the milestone during his first three seasons after Joe DiMaggio and Judge. Rice's plate appearances often prompt a rendition of Elton John's "Bennie and the Jets″ from the stadium's organist, and Rice has sparked an often struggling offense with 16 go-ahead homers this year and three that have tied games.
“One thing I always tell guys the difference between minor leaguers and big leaguers is the consistency,” Judge said. “He’s one of the best. I can look up at the clock and I know exactly where he’s going to be in the cage. You know what he’s doing in the training room, the weight room. It’s just every single day, man, this guy’s a machine.”
A 12th-round pick in the 2021 amateur draft from Dartmouth, where he played just 30 games over three years due to the coronavirus pandemic, Rice was mostly a catcher but occasionally a first baseman in the minors. He made his big league debut in June 2024 at age 25 after Anthony Rizzo broke a forearm.
Rice hit .171 with seven homers and 23 RBIs in 50 games that year, then batted .255 with 26 homers and 65 RBIs in 138 games last year.
With Stanton sidelined for most of the season, the left-handed-hitting Rice has 93 games at DH this year and 52 at first.
“It's tough to pull him off his back leg,” Yankees pitcher Gerrit Cole said. “He’s really able to stay balanced and deliver high-efficacy strikes on various pitches in all parts of the zone.”
Rice was hitting .306 through May, then batted .196 in June. An 18-for-58 (.119) slide after the All-Star break dropped his season average to .248 on Aug. 22 but he's rebounded to bat .333 (34 for 102) since.
“Went through a lull, which is inevitable, even in a great season,” Boone said. “Had a stretch in there where it was a struggle and he was grinding but kind of battled through that and feel like the last few weeks has been on a really good run.”
Rice's potential was evident on July 6, 2024, less than a month into his big league career, when he became the first Yankees rookie with three home runs in a game and tied Lou Gehrig's Yankees rookie record of seven RBIs. Consistency took time.
“A lot of it I always feel like is just experience-based,” Rice said. “You just see more pitching at the big league level, get exposed to guys who throw all different kinds of pitches from different angles and slots and all these things. I feel like I’ve always been a good learner in that way.”
